first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_86 and memory_31 both demonstrate that onboarding simplification and signup field reduction drive durable activation lifts in self-serve segments. Verifying these two records will confirm the mechanisms and effect sizes before committing. Simplify_onboarding targets the root metric degradation directly rather than chasing competitor pricing (which memory_73 shows is retention-destructive) or premature referral programs. Activation_messaging (memory_91) also proved effective, but onboarding simplification addresses the completion dropout earlier in the funnel. Enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to the current SMB-weighted activation crisis. Standard_experiment scale is appropriate for a high-confidence directional play with verified precedent. This preserves the option to pivot if verification reveals contextual differences, while addressing sustainable long-term qualified revenue through improved core product adoption rather than margin-eroding tactics.

mid.rationale: Verification confirms both onboarding simplification mechanisms. Exp_86 shows +13% completion lift with +3% retention and -2.1 day time-to-value improvement. Exp_31 shows +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue lift on SMB with minimal retention risk (-1%). Current state: onboarding completion down 4% QoQ, activation down 6% QoQ. Simplify_onboarding directly targets these metrics and has demonstrated durable qualified revenue impact. SMB segment remains price-sensitive (competitor pressure ongoing), making retention-safe activation improvement the highest-leverage lever. Standard_experiment scale allows measurement of effect size and segment applicability before broad rollout. Avoids memory_73 pitfall (promotional_pricing materially reduced 30-day retention). Preserves uncertainty about whether onboarding degradation is flow-specific or demand-side; experiment will clarify. Primary objective of maximizing sustainable long-term qualified revenue is best served by proven activation mechanism rather than margin-destructive competitor matching.

final2.rationale: Pressure to match competitor pricing is real, but memory_73 explicitly warns: promotional pricing materially reduced 30-day retention and should not be generalized as growth strategy. Matching a second price cut would likely cause greater retention harm on already-churning SMB base. Simplify_onboarding remains the highest-confidence lever: verified +13% completion, +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue with minimal retention risk. Activation and onboarding completion remain down 4-6% QoQ; this gap has not closed. SMB churn conversations are about price, but competitive pricing races destroy margin and lock in commoditization. The counter-move is to increase perceived value and reduce friction to activation—proving product stickiness through faster time-to-value and completion. Scaling to small_guarded_test (rather than standard) allows rapid iteration if market response demands urgency, while preserving measurement integrity. If onboarding simplification lifts qualified revenue and activation within 3-4 days, it provides a defensible narrative to leadership that value-building beats price-matching. Referral_incentive is untested on SMB segment specifically. Enterprise_sales_assist does not address SMB churn. Activation_messaging alone is insufficient without the funnel cleanup that onboarding simplification provides.
